intro: Welcome! Today you write about yourself in English: who you are, your family and your day, and then a short message or postcard to a friend. You already know the grammar; now we make it look right on paper, with capital letters and full stops in the right places.
teachingNotes: Writing about yourself uses only what the learner knows: am/is/are for facts about a person (I'm 24. I'm a nurse. My mother is a teacher.) and the simple present for what people do (I live in Bandung. My sister works in a bank. I get up at six.). Organise it as me → my family → my routine, and join ideas with and, but and because.

Common grammar errors in writing: no -s with he/she/it (*'My father work in a hotel'), be + verb (*'My sister is live in Bogor', *'I am work'), have instead of has (*'My brother have a car'). Indonesian has no 'am/is/are' and no verb endings, so check both in every sentence.

Capitals: the main error is chat style, everything in small letters: 'i live in bandung.' → 'I live in Bandung.' Capitals for the first word, I (always), names (Rina, Pak Hasan), places, days (Monday), months (June), languages and nationalities (English, Indonesian). Not for jobs (teacher), seasons (summer) or my/me. In 'Dear Mum,' Mum is used like a name, so it has a capital; in 'my mum' it doesn't.

Punctuation: one idea, one sentence. Indonesian learners often join two sentences with a comma or with nothing (*'I live in Medan, I work in a bank'): use a full stop and a capital, or join with and/but. A comma after the greeting (Dear Tom, / Hi Andi,) and after the ending word (Love, / Best wishes,) before the name; a comma before but when it joins two sentences. One exclamation mark is friendly; not on every sentence.

Short messages and postcards (25–35 words): greeting (Dear… for anyone, Hi… for friends), 2–4 short sentences, an ending (Love, for family and close friends; Best wishes, for anyone, also a boss or teacher; See you soon! / Write soon! as fixed friendly phrases) and the name. Words are counted between spaces: I'm counts as one word, the greeting and the name count too. British Mum = American Mom.

Limits (A1): no past simple (a postcard says 'The beach is beautiful. Every morning we swim.', not 'Yesterday we visited…'), no future (will, going to), no present perfect; avoid the present continuous and there is/are, which are not in this lesson's path. Don't teach formal letters (Yours sincerely) or paragraphs beyond 3–5 short sentences.

keyPoints.title: Sentences about you, your family and your routine
keyPoints.explanation: Use am/is/are to say who someone is (I'm a nurse. My mother is a teacher.) and the simple present to say what they do (I live in Bandung. I get up at six.). For one other person (he, she, my sister) the verb takes -s: my sister lives, my father works; have becomes has. Never put am/is/are before another verb: not 'I am work'.

examples.en: I get up at six every day.
examples.id: Aku bangun jam enam setiap hari.

id.title: Kalimat tentang dirimu, keluargamu dan rutinitasmu
id.explanation: Pakai am/is/are untuk mengatakan siapa seseorang (I'm a nurse. My mother is a teacher.) dan simple present untuk mengatakan apa yang dia lakukan (I live in Bandung. I get up at six.). Untuk satu orang lain (he, she, my sister) kata kerjanya ditambah -s: my sister lives, my father works; have menjadi has. Jangan taruh am/is/are sebelum kata kerja lain: bukan 'I am work'.

keyPoints.title: A short message or postcard
keyPoints.explanation: A message or postcard of 25–35 words has three parts: a greeting (Dear Mum, / Hi Andi,), 2–4 short sentences, and an ending with your name (Love, for family and close friends; Best wishes, for anyone). Use the simple present and am/is/are: The hotel is nice. Every morning we swim.

examples.en: The hotel is small but nice.

id.title: Pesan atau kartu pos pendek
id.explanation: Pesan atau kartu pos 25–35 kata punya tiga bagian: salam pembuka (Dear Mum, / Hi Andi,), 2–4 kalimat pendek, dan penutup dengan namamu (Love, untuk keluarga dan sahabat; Best wishes, untuk siapa saja). Pakai simple present dan am/is/are: The hotel is nice. Every morning we swim.

keyPoints.title: Capital letters and punctuation
keyPoints.explanation: Capital letters for the first word, I, names, places, days, months, languages and nationalities. One idea, one sentence: end it with a full stop and start the next with a capital; don't join two sentences with a comma. Put a comma after the greeting and after the ending word.

examples.id: Aku tinggal di Bandung. (bukan: i live in bandung.)

examples.en: I live in Medan. I work in a bank.
examples.id: Aku tinggal di Medan. Aku bekerja di bank. (dua kalimat, bukan dipisah koma)

id.title: Huruf kapital dan tanda baca
id.explanation: Huruf kapital untuk kata pertama, I, nama orang, tempat, hari, bulan, bahasa dan kebangsaan. Satu ide, satu kalimat: akhiri dengan titik dan mulai kalimat berikutnya dengan huruf kapital; jangan gabungkan dua kalimat dengan koma. Taruh koma setelah salam pembuka dan setelah kata penutup.

assessment.prompt: Use the notes to write one sentence: my brother / work / in a bank / in Jakarta
acceptableAnswers: my brother works in a bank in jakarta
my brother works at a bank in jakarta
assessment.rubric: Correct: My brother works in a bank in Jakarta. 'work' without -s = 40. 'is work' or 'is works' = 30. Missing capitals (my, jakarta) = minus 20.

assessment.prompt: Correct the mistake: My mother is cook breakfast every morning.
acceptableAnswers: my mother cooks breakfast every morning
every morning my mother cooks breakfast
assessment.rubric: Correct: My mother cooks breakfast every morning. Removing 'is' but keeping 'cook' (no -s) = 50. 'is cooking' = 30. 'My mother is a cook' (different meaning) = 0.

assessment.prompt: Use the notes to write one sentence: Pak Hasan / have / three children
acceptableAnswers: pak hasan has got three children
assessment.rubric: Correct: Pak Hasan has three children. 'have' instead of 'has' = 40. 'childrens' or 'child' = minus 30.

assessment.prompt: Write the words that need a capital letter: on saturday i visit my aunt in bogor.
assessment.rubric: Correct: On, Saturday, I, Bogor (any order). Each missing or extra word = minus 25 ('aunt' and 'my' are not capitals).

assessment.prompt: This message needs one more full stop. Write the word that comes just before it: My name is Dewi I'm a nurse in Medan.
assessment.rubric: Correct: Dewi (My name is Dewi. I'm a nurse in Medan.). Any other word = 0.

assessment.prompt: You write a postcard to your friend Lisa. Write the greeting (the first line).
assessment.rubric: Correct: Dear Lisa, / Hi Lisa, / Hello Lisa,. Only 'Lisa' = 50. A greeting without the name = 50. 'lisa' with a small l = minus 20.

assessment.prompt: Put the parts of this postcard in the right order. Write the letters. A: Love, Dimas  B: Hi Nadia,  C: See you soon!  D: I'm in Lombok with my family. The beach is beautiful.
assessment.rubric: Correct: B, D, C, A. Greeting first and name last but C and D swapped = 60. Any other order = 0.

material.title: Sentences about you, your family and your day

blocks.text:
When you write about yourself, you need two things you already know.

- **am / is / are** to say who or what someone is: *I'm 24. I'm a nurse. My mother is a teacher.*
- the **simple present** to say what someone does: *I live in Bandung. I work in a bank. I get up at six.*

A good order is: **me → my family → my day**. Keep each sentence short, and join two ideas with **and**, **but** or **because**.

id.text:
Saat menulis tentang dirimu, kamu butuh dua hal yang sudah kamu pelajari.

- **am / is / are** untuk mengatakan siapa atau apa seseorang: *I'm 24. I'm a nurse. My mother is a teacher.*
- **simple present** untuk mengatakan apa yang seseorang lakukan: *I live in Bandung. I work in a bank. I get up at six.*

Urutan yang enak: **aku → keluargaku → hariku**. Buat setiap kalimat pendek, dan gabungkan dua ide dengan **and**, **but** atau **because**.

rows.en: My name is Sari and I'm 24.
I'm a nurse in Bandung.
rows.note: a nurse: English needs a/an before a job

id.note: a nurse: bahasa Inggris butuh a/an sebelum pekerjaan

rows.en: My sister lives in Bogor.
My father has a small shop.
rows.note: have → has: an exception to remember

id.note: have → has: pengecualian yang harus dihafal

rows.en: I get up at six and I go to work by bus.
rows.id: Aku bangun jam enam dan berangkat kerja naik bus.

blocks.text: **Two Indonesian traps.** Indonesian says *Saya perawat* with no extra word, but English needs **am**: *I **am** a nurse*. And Indonesian verbs never change, but in English one other person (he, she, my sister, Pak Hasan) takes **-s**: *my sister live**s***, *my father work**s***. This -s doesn't mean 'many'. The two never go together: not *I am work*, not *She is live in Bogor*. Use **am/is/are** only when there is no other verb.

id.text: **Dua jebakan dari bahasa Indonesia.** Bahasa Indonesia bilang *Saya perawat* tanpa kata tambahan, tapi bahasa Inggris butuh **am**: *I **am** a nurse*. Lalu kata kerja Indonesia tidak pernah berubah, tapi dalam bahasa Inggris satu orang lain (he, she, my sister, Pak Hasan) memakai **-s**: *my sister live**s***, *my father work**s***. Huruf -s ini tidak berarti 'banyak'. Keduanya tidak pernah dipakai bersama: bukan *I am work*, bukan *She is live in Bogor*. Pakai **am/is/are** hanya kalau tidak ada kata kerja lain.

blocks.explain: My brother = he, one person, so have becomes has. 'is have' is wrong because am/is/are never goes before another verb.

id.explain: My brother = he, satu orang, jadi have menjadi has. 'is have' salah karena am/is/are tidak pernah diletakkan sebelum kata kerja lain.

id.title: Kalimat tentang dirimu, keluargamu dan harimu

blocks.text:
Use a **capital letter** for:

- the **first word** of every sentence
- **I** (always, even in the middle of a sentence)
- **names** of people: *Rina, Pak Hasan, Bu Ani*
- **places**: *Bandung, Jalan Braga, Indonesia*
- **days** and **months**: *Monday, Saturday, June, August*
- **languages** and **nationalities**: *English, Indonesian, Japanese*

Most of this is the same in Indonesian (*Senin, Juni, bahasa Inggris*). The new one is **I**.

id.text:
Pakai **huruf kapital** untuk:

- **kata pertama** setiap kalimat
- **I** (selalu, bahkan di tengah kalimat)
- **nama** orang: *Rina, Pak Hasan, Bu Ani*
- **tempat**: *Bandung, Jalan Braga, Indonesia*
- **hari** dan **bulan**: *Monday, Saturday, June, August*
- **bahasa** dan **kebangsaan**: *English, Indonesian, Japanese*

Sebagian besar sama dengan bahasa Indonesia (*Senin, Juni, bahasa Inggris*). Yang baru adalah **I**.

rows.en: I live in Bandung.
Budi and I speak Indonesian and English.
rows.id: Budi dan aku bisa bahasa Indonesia dan bahasa Inggris.
rows.note: I in the middle, two languages: capitals

id.note: I di tengah kalimat, dua bahasa: huruf kapital

rows.en: My birthday is on 3 March.
My mother is a teacher.

blocks.text:
**What stays small:** jobs (*teacher, nurse*), seasons (*summer*; Indonesia has *musim hujan* and *musim kemarau*, both small), and **my** and **me** (only **I** is special). **Mum** is small in *my mum*, but in *Dear Mum,* you use it like her name, so it gets a capital. (*Mum* is British; American English writes *Mom*.)

In chat apps people type *i live in bandung*. In a message to a new friend, an email or a postcard, use capitals: a small *i* looks like a mistake.

id.text:
**Yang tetap huruf kecil:** pekerjaan (*teacher, nurse*), musim (*summer*; di Indonesia ada *musim hujan* dan *musim kemarau*, keduanya huruf kecil), dan **my** serta **me** (hanya **I** yang istimewa). **Mum** ditulis kecil di *my mum*, tapi di *Dear Mum,* kamu memakainya seperti nama ibumu, jadi diawali kapital. (*Mum* itu British; bahasa Inggris Amerika menulis *Mom*.)

Di aplikasi chat orang mengetik *i live in bandung*. Di pesan untuk teman baru, email atau kartu pos, pakai huruf kapital: huruf *i* kecil terlihat seperti kesalahan.

blocks.prompt: Which word does NOT need a capital letter?
blocks.explain: Teacher is a job, not a name, so it stays small. Monday is a day and English is a language: both always have a capital.

id.prompt: Kata mana yang TIDAK perlu huruf kapital?
id.explain: Teacher adalah pekerjaan, bukan nama, jadi tetap huruf kecil. Monday adalah hari dan English adalah bahasa: keduanya selalu diawali huruf kapital.

blocks.text:
A **sentence** is one complete idea: who + what (*I work in a bank.*). End it with a **full stop** (.) and start the next sentence with a **capital letter**. Don't join two sentences with a **comma** (,) or with nothing, like many people do in chat. If the two ideas belong together, join them with **and** or **but**.

Other marks you need in a message:

- a **comma** after the greeting (*Dear Andi,*) and after the ending word (*Love,* / *Best wishes,*), before your name
- a **comma** before **but** when it joins two sentences (*The hotel is small, but it's clean.*)
- an **exclamation mark** (!) to sound friendly (*See you soon!*). One is enough; don't put it on every sentence.

id.text:
**Kalimat** adalah satu ide yang lengkap: siapa + apa (*I work in a bank.*). Akhiri dengan **full stop** (titik .) dan mulai kalimat berikutnya dengan **huruf kapital**. Jangan gabungkan dua kalimat dengan **koma** (,) atau tanpa tanda apa pun, seperti yang sering orang lakukan di chat. Kalau dua ide itu memang berhubungan, gabungkan dengan **and** atau **but**.

Tanda lain yang kamu perlukan dalam pesan:

- **koma** setelah salam pembuka (*Dear Andi,*) dan setelah kata penutup (*Love,* / *Best wishes,*), sebelum namamu
- **koma** sebelum **but** saat menggabungkan dua kalimat (*The hotel is small, but it's clean.*)
- **tanda seru** (!) supaya terdengar ramah (*See you soon!*). Satu saja cukup; jangan dipakai di setiap kalimat.

rows.en: I live in Medan. I work in a bank.
rows.id: Aku tinggal di Medan. Aku bekerja di bank.

rows.en: I live in Medan and I work in a bank.
rows.id: Aku tinggal di Medan dan bekerja di bank.

rows.en: My flat is small, but it's near my office.

blocks.text: **The comma trap.** In Indonesian chat, *aku tinggal di Medan, kerja di bank* looks fine. In English, *I live in Medan, I work in a bank* is a mistake: two complete ideas need a full stop or **and**. Read your text aloud: where your voice stops and goes down, put a full stop.

id.text: **Jebakan koma.** Di chat bahasa Indonesia, *aku tinggal di Medan, kerja di bank* terlihat wajar. Dalam bahasa Inggris, *I live in Medan, I work in a bank* adalah kesalahan: dua ide lengkap butuh titik atau **and**. Baca tulisanmu dengan suara keras: di tempat suaramu berhenti dan turun, taruh titik.

blocks.prompt: What can you use between two complete sentences?
options: a full stop, or the word and
blocks.explain: Two complete ideas need a full stop (then a capital) or a joining word like and: I live in Medan. I work in a bank. / I live in Medan and I work in a bank. A comma alone is a mistake in English.

id.prompt: Apa yang bisa kamu pakai di antara dua kalimat lengkap?
id.explain: Dua ide lengkap butuh titik (lalu huruf kapital) atau kata penghubung seperti and: I live in Medan. I work in a bank. / I live in Medan and I work in a bank. Koma saja adalah kesalahan dalam bahasa Inggris.

blocks.text:
A short message or postcard (**25–35 words**) has three parts:

- a **greeting**: *Dear Mum,* (good for anyone) or *Hi Andi,* (for friends)
- **2–4 short sentences**: where you are, what it's like, what you do, or a little about you
- an **ending** and your **name**: *Love,* (family and close friends) or *Best wishes,* (anyone, also a teacher or a boss). *See you soon!* and *Write soon!* (balas ya) are friendly fixed phrases before the ending.

To **count words**, count everything between spaces: *I'm* is one word, and the greeting and your name count too.

id.text:
Pesan pendek atau kartu pos (**25–35 kata**) punya tiga bagian:

- **salam pembuka**: *Dear Mum,* (cocok untuk siapa saja) atau *Hi Andi,* (untuk teman)
- **2–4 kalimat pendek**: kamu di mana, tempatnya seperti apa, apa yang kamu lakukan, atau sedikit tentang dirimu
- **penutup** dan **namamu**: *Love,* (keluarga dan sahabat) atau *Best wishes,* (siapa saja, juga guru atau atasan). *See you soon!* (sampai ketemu!) dan *Write soon!* (balas ya!) adalah ungkapan tetap yang ramah sebelum penutup.

Untuk **menghitung kata**, hitung semua yang dipisah spasi: *I'm* dihitung satu kata, dan salam pembuka serta namamu juga dihitung.

rows.en: Dear Mum,
I'm in Bali with Sari. The hotel is small but nice.
rows.id: Aku di Bali bersama Sari. Hotelnya kecil tapi bagus.
rows.note: where you are, what it's like

id.note: kamu di mana, tempatnya seperti apa

rows.en: Every morning we swim in the sea, and in the evening we eat at a warung.
rows.id: Setiap pagi kami berenang di laut, dan malamnya kami makan di warung.

id.note: apa yang kamu lakukan: simple present

rows.en: The food is delicious!
Love, Rina
Hi Emma,
rows.note: a message to a new friend

rows.en: My name is Budi and I'm 23. I live in Surabaya with my parents and my sister.
rows.id: Namaku Budi dan umurku 23 tahun. Aku tinggal di Surabaya bersama orang tua dan adik perempuanku.

rows.en: I work in a hotel. I love football, and I play every Sunday.
rows.id: Aku bekerja di hotel. Aku suka sekali sepak bola, dan aku main setiap hari Minggu.

rows.en: Write soon! Budi

blocks.text: **Postcards use the present here.** Write what is true now and what you do every day: *The beach is beautiful. Every morning we swim.* You don't need other tenses for a good A1 postcard. And keep it friendly but not too private: no address or phone number on a postcard anyone can read.

id.text: **Di sini kartu pos memakai bentuk present.** Tulis apa yang benar sekarang dan apa yang kamu lakukan setiap hari: *The beach is beautiful. Every morning we swim.* Kamu tidak perlu tenses lain untuk kartu pos A1 yang bagus. Dan buat ramah tapi jangan terlalu pribadi: jangan tulis alamat atau nomor HP di kartu pos yang bisa dibaca siapa saja.

blocks.prompt: How many words are in this message? Hi Andi, I'm at home. See you soon! Budi
blocks.explain: Count everything between spaces: Hi, Andi, I'm, at, home, See, you, soon, Budi = 9. I'm is one word (not two), and the greeting and the name count too.

id.prompt: Berapa jumlah kata dalam pesan ini? Hi Andi, I'm at home. See you soon! Budi
id.explain: Hitung semua yang dipisah spasi: Hi, Andi, I'm, at, home, See, you, soon, Budi = 9. I'm dihitung satu kata (bukan dua), dan salam pembuka serta nama juga dihitung.
